questions.question:
Select the option that will correctly replace the question mark (?) in the series.

JMP, NOQ, RQR, ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f0a3e32b57e2393fbe73836962f87739b4ab822af37a0422d586f9f9d371458.png] 

First letter in each term,

J + 4 → N; N + 4 → R; R + 4 → **V**

Second letter in each term,

M + 2 → O; O + 2 → Q; Q + 2 → **S**

Third letter in each term,

P + 1 → Q; Q + 1 → R; R + 1 → **S**

Hence, the fourth term in the series will be **VSS.**

questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established fact, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:** 

All tables are TVs.

All TVs are gates.

**Conclusion:**

I: Some Gates are tables.

II: All tables are gates

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for given statements is:

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/960cbe35047516075cf8ea0409ae19383364e7793242e2fe5ce84813f1be2d97.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I: Some gates are tables → True (from the figure)

II: All tables are gate → True (from the figure)

Hence, both the conclusions follow

questions.question:

If P = Q + R – T, then how is P related to T?
questions.solution:
Given code: P = Q + R – T

Explanation: P is mother of Q. Q is Father of R. R is son of T.

Preparing the family tree using the following symbols,

Hence, P is the mother-in-law of T.

questions.question: In a certain code, CODE is written as 900. How will RACE be written in that code?
questions.solution:
Logic for CODE is,

C × O × D × E = 3 × 15 × 4 × 5 = 900

Similarly,

R × A × C × E = 18 × 1 × 3 × 5 = **270**.

Hence, code for RACE is **270**.

questions.question:
What will come in place of the blank in the given series?

4, 12, 36, 108, 324, ________, 2916
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Each number is multiplied by 3 to get the next number in series.

4 × 3 = 12

12 × 3 = 36

36 × 3 = 108

108 × 3 = 324

324 × 3 = **972**

972 × 3 = 2916

Hence, the missing term in the series in **972**.

questions.question: What day did 6th August 1987 fall on?
questions.solution:
To determine the day of the week on 6th August 1987, we use the following method:

 
• 1987 = 1600 + 300 years (1601 to 1900) + 86 years (1901 to 1986) + year 1987
 
• No. of odd days from 1601 to 1900 = 1 odd day (5 odd days in every 100 years)
 
• The total number of odd days from 1901 to 1986 = 21 leap years + 65 ordinary years = 42 + 65 = 107 odd days = 2 odd days.
 
• In 1600 years, odd days = 0
 
• So total in 1986 years = 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 odd days 

 
 

 
 
Month (1987)

 
 
 
No. of odd days = no. of days in the month (mod 7)

 
 
 

 
 
January

• In 1987, the no. of days up to 6 August = 31(Jan) + 28 (Feb) + 31(Mar) + 30(Apr) + 31(May) + 30(June) + 31(July) + 6 days (Aug) = 218/7 = 1 odd days. 

Therefore, total no. of odd days up to 6th August 1987 = 3 + 1 = 4

Now, if the remainder (the total no. of odd days) is as follows, then it corresponds to the following day:

• We have remainder 4 which corresponds to Thursday.

Hence, on 6th August 1987, it was a Thursday.
